name: Privatrak Analytics
author: privatrak

sections.description:
Privatrak shows you what people do on your site, not only which pages they open.

As soon as you add your website key, Privatrak names the clicks that matter: your menus, the search, comment and contact forms, and add-to-cart buttons. Privatrak calls these features. Each comes with details, such as the menu a link is in, or the product a button adds and its price. You see which features people use, and you can build a funnel that shows where shoppers drop off between the cart and the purchase.

In a WooCommerce shop, make the order a goal and Privatrak shows the orders and the revenue of every source and campaign, so you see which newsletter, ad or search engine brings sales.

Privatrak sets no cookies and stores nothing on your visitors’ devices. It is built to run without a consent banner.

This plugin connects your site to a Privatrak project. You need a Privatrak account, which you can create for free at privatrak.com.

What Privatrak records on your site

  • The clicks that matter, recorded as features with their details, ready to use in funnels.
  • Clicks that go wrong, which Privatrak calls click problems: buttons that do nothing, that people click again and again, that respond slowly or that cause an error.
  • Each completed WooCommerce order, as a custom event called Purchase. It carries the order’s total, currency and number of items, and nothing about the customer. Use it as a goal, with the total as its value, to see revenue per source and campaign.
  • Any other button you choose. Open the Element Picker from your Privatrak project, click the button on your site and give it a name. No code needed.
  • Every page view and click, recorded automatically.
  • The trait signed-in for visitors who are signed in to your site, so you can compare them with everyone else. On sites translated with Polylang or WPML, a trait for the page’s language, such as language-de.

Privatrak leaves out anyone who can write or edit posts on your site, including you. You can still use the Element Picker and the Click Map on your site while you are signed in.

AI services and crawlers

AI services such as ChatGPT or Claude read your pages to answer people’s questions without running JavaScript, so a tracker in the page never sees them. Switch on Count AI services and crawlers that don’t run JavaScript under Settings › Privatrak, and your site tells Privatrak about each request from a known crawler. Privatrak then shows which AI services read which of your pages.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Privatrak (https://privatrak.com), a web analytics service. It sends nothing until you save a website key under Settings › Privatrak.

The tracker. Once a key is saved, every page of your site loads the tracker from api.privatrak.com. While a visitor is on a page, the tracker sends Privatrak:

  • the address of the page, and of the site the visitor came from;
  • for each click, the button or link clicked, its text, and the feature name and details this plugin gives it;
  • for a click that goes wrong, which kind of problem it was, and for a script error only its type, such as TypeError, never its message;
  • the time of each page view and click;
  • the traits this plugin adds: signed-in for visitors signed in to your site, and the page’s language on multilingual sites;
  • on the WooCommerce order confirmation page, the order’s total, currency and number of items.

The tracker never reads what visitors type into forms.

Each request also carries the visitor’s IP address and browser version, as every request on the web does. Privatrak uses them only to recognise the same visitor within one day. It does not store them.

The key check. When you open Settings › Privatrak, your browser asks api.privatrak.com whether the saved key belongs to a project. It sends only the key.

AI services and crawlers. Only if you switch on Count AI services and crawlers that don’t run JavaScript, your site itself contacts api.privatrak.com, and only when a request comes from a known crawler, such as ChatGPT or Claude reading a page. For each such request it sends:

  • the address of the page, without its query string, after your project’s privacy settings in Privatrak have removed anything private from it;
  • the name the crawler gives itself (its User-Agent);
  • the time of the request, to the second;
  • your website key.

It never sends anything about your visitors or their IP addresses. To know what counts as a crawler and how to treat addresses, your site also downloads the list of crawler names from api.privatrak.com once a day, and your project’s privacy settings every ten minutes, only while crawlers are visiting. A copy of the list comes with the plugin.

The Element Picker and the Click Map. When you open one of them on your site from your Privatrak project, your browser loads it from api.privatrak.com. Nothing is recorded while it is open.

The service is subject to Privatrak’s terms of service and privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins › Add Plugin, search for Privatrak and click Install Now, then Activate.
  2. In your Privatrak project, open Settings › API Keys and copy the key of type Your website.
  3. In WordPress, go to Settings › Privatrak, paste the key into Website key and click Save Changes.

The settings page then checks the key and tells you whether it is connected.

If your project lists allowed domains, add your site’s domain under Settings › Privacy › Allowed domains in Privatrak. The settings page shows you which domain that is.
sections.faq:
Does Privatrak use cookies or store anything on visitors’ devices?

No. Privatrak sets no cookies and stores nothing on your visitors’ devices, and the details this plugin sends contain no personal data. It is built to run without a consent banner.

If you add details of your own to buttons on your site, keep personal data such as email addresses out of them.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. Cached pages carry the tracker like the rest of the page.

Some speed plugins combine, delay or rewrite JavaScript, with settings such as Combine JavaScript or Delay JavaScript. Such a setting can stop Privatrak from recording anything. If it does, add tracker.js to the list of files that setting leaves alone.

Which clicks become features without any setup?

On every WordPress site:

  • Menu links, in classic and block themes, as the feature Navigation, with the link’s text and the menu as details.
  • The search button, as Search.
  • The comment form, as Comment.

With these plugins:

  • WooCommerce: add-to-cart buttons as Add to cart, with the product’s name, number, category and price. Products with sizes or other variations have no single price until the shopper picks one, so their buttons come without it. Product reviews as Review. Each completed order as a custom event called Purchase.
  • Contact Form 7: the submit button as Contact form, with the form’s title.
  • Polylang and WPML: a trait for the page’s language, such as language-de.

Feature names are always in English, whatever language your site is in.

What about other plugins?

Privatrak records every page view and click on your site, whatever else you have installed. Clicks on buttons from other plugins, such as form builders and page builders, arrive with the text of the button or link.

To give them a feature name, open the Element Picker from your Privatrak project and click the button on your site. Developers can add a data-track attribute instead.

Write to support@privatrak.com if you would like Privatrak to name actions from another plugin, or if you need help.

My site already uses the `data-track` attribute. What happens to it?

Your data-track attributes stay as they are.

The plugin’s feature names take priority over feature rules you created in Privatrak for the same clicks. This applies to clicks recorded while Record common actions as features is on. To keep your own rules for those clicks, switch it off.

Why don’t I see my own clicks?

Privatrak leaves out anyone who can write or edit posts. To see your clicks recorded, open your site in a private browser window.

While you are signed in, you can still use the Element Picker and the Click Map on your site.

How many trait keys does the plugin use?

One for signed-in, and one for each language on a multilingual site. To use none, switch off Tell signed-in visitors apart.

Can Privatrak count AI services such as ChatGPT that read my pages?

Yes, once you switch on Count AI services and crawlers that don’t run JavaScript under Settings › Privatrak. It is off until you do.

AI services such as ChatGPT or Claude read a page without running its JavaScript, so the tracker never sees them. With the setting on, your site recognises requests from known crawlers by the name they give themselves and tells Privatrak about each one: the address of the page and that name. Nothing is sent for your visitors.

A caching plugin answers most of these requests from its cache, before WordPress runs, and those are not counted. So behind a page cache the real numbers can be higher. We checked WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache and LiteSpeed Cache: with their usual settings, all three answer AI services and crawlers from the cache.

Can I load the tracker from my own domain?

Yes. In wp-config.php, set PRIVATRAK_SCRIPT_URL to the address you serve tracker.js from, and PRIVATRAK_API_HOST to the address of the Privatrak API.

Serve tracker-picker.js from the same folder as tracker.js. The Element Picker and the Click Map load it from there.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • No change to the plugin. The description now explains how to count your WooCommerce orders as a goal in Privatrak, with the orders and the revenue of every source and campaign.

1.1.0

  • New setting, off until you switch it on: count AI services such as ChatGPT and Claude, and other crawlers that don’t run JavaScript, when they read your pages.

1.0.0

  • First release.

A dashboard in Privatrak for a WooCommerce shop: revenue, orders and the average order, visits from a sale campaign, and which products go into the cart.
